# ui::WindowOptions

Header: `winui/ui/WindowOptions.hpp`.

What a [Window](window.md) is created with: title, size, theme, frame, placement and the per-window services. A [Window](window.md) owns one, given to its constructor. `title`, `theme`, `backdrop` and `icon` take a value or a property: bound to a property, the window follows it for as long as both live, so one `ui::Property<ui::ThemeRequest>` can drive every window of an app. `style`, `chrome`, `system_menu` and the size limits seed the [Window](window.md)'s own live properties (set_style(), ...), which is where to change them afterwards; the rest is read once, when the OS window is created by [ui::run()](namespace-ui.md#run) or [Window::show()](window.md#show).

A bound field subscribes to its properties while the [Window](window.md) is constructed. A [Window](window.md) that is a class member therefore has to be declared after the properties it binds, since members are constructed in declaration order; bound to a member declared later, it reads an object that does not exist yet.

Example: 
```cpp
int main()
{
    ui::Property<ui::ThemeRequest> theme{{.mode = ui::ThemeMode::Dark}};
    ui::Window window{{
        .title    = "My Application",
        .size     = {1024, 768},
        .theme    = theme, // every window bound to `theme` switches with it
        .backdrop = ui::Backdrop::Mica,
        .min_size = {480, 320},
    }};
    window.set_content(ui::Text{.text = "Hello"});
    return ui::run(window);
}
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `Binding<std::string>` |  | The caption and taskbar text, UTF-8; [Window::title()](window.md#title). Bound, the window follows it. |
| `size` | `Size` | `{800.0f, 600.0f}` | The client area's size in DIPs, the room the content gets, whatever frame the theme draws around it; scaled by DPI at creation. |
| `theme` | `Binding<ThemeRequest>` |  | What to resolve the live [Theme](../themes/theme.md) from; [Window::set_theme()](window.md#set_theme). Defaults to ThemeMode::System, which follows the OS light/dark, accent and high-contrast settings as they change. Bound, the window follows it (a pin_theme() in between is undone by the next change). A designated list needs its type here: `.theme = ui::ThemeRequest{.mode = ...}`. |
| `backdrop` | `Binding<Backdrop>` | `{Backdrop::None}` | Opt-in system backdrop material ([ui::Backdrop](namespace-ui.md#backdrop)); [Window::set_backdrop()](window.md#set_backdrop). Bound, the window follows it. |
| `style` | `WindowStyle` |  | The frame ([ui::WindowStyle](window-style.md)). The defaults give a plain resizable window with a caption, a system menu and minimize and maximize buttons. Seeds [Window::set_style()](window.md#set_style); change it live through the [Window](window.md) afterwards. |
| `spell_check` | `SpellCheckOptions` |  | See [`SpellCheckOptions`](spell-check-options.md) above. |
| `initial_state` | `WindowState` | `WindowState::Normal` | The state to show in. `Normal` honors the launcher, so a shortcut set to "Run: Maximized" or "Minimized" still gets its way. |
| `position` | `std::optional<Point>` |  | Top-left of the window, in DIPs of the primary monitor. Absent lets the system cascade it. |
| `min_size` | `Size` |  | Smallest client size the user can drag the window to, in DIPs; zero on an axis leaves it unconstrained. Not applied while full screen. |
| `max_size` | `Size` |  | Largest client size, in DIPs; zero on an axis leaves it unconstrained. |
| `placement` | `std::optional<WindowPlacement>` |  | A placement saved from [Window::placement()](window.md#placement) on a previous run. Overrides `initial_state` and `position`. The system pulls it back on screen if its monitor is gone. |
| `chrome` | `ChromeOverrides` |  | Seeds [Window::set_chrome()](window.md#set_chrome): this window's own frame colors and corners over the theme's. |
| `icon` | `Binding<std::optional<WindowIcon>>` |  | The caption and taskbar icon; [Window::set_icon()](window.md#set_icon). Absent uses the executable's first icon resource, the one the file manager shows for the file, or the system's default without one. [`ui::WindowIcon{.resource = "#101"}`](window-icon.md) picks another of the executable's icons. Bound, the window follows it. |
| `system_menu` | `std::vector<MenuItem>` |  | Seeds [Window::set_system_menu()](window.md#set_system_menu) when non-empty. |
| `taskbar_progress` | `Binding<TaskbarProgress>` |  | The progress the taskbar button shows; [Window::taskbar_progress()](window.md#taskbar_progress), which also sets it after construction. Bound, the button follows it, such as a job's progress while it runs. A [Window](window.md) class member binds only properties declared before it (see WindowOptions). Example:  ```cpp ui::Property<double> done{0.0}; // the export's progress, 0 to 1 ui::Window window{{     .title            = "Export",     .taskbar_progress = ui::bind(done, [](double f) {         const auto state = f < 1.0 ? ui::TaskbarProgressState::Normal : ui::TaskbarProgressState::None;         return ui::TaskbarProgress{state, f};     }), }}; ``` |
| `owner` | `Window*` | `nullptr` | The window this one belongs to: an owned window stays above its owner, minimizes and closes with it, and has no taskbar button of its own. nullptr: none. |
| `modal` | `bool` | `false` | With an `owner`: the owner takes no input while this window is open, and gets the activation back when it closes. Ignored without one. |
| `visible` | `bool` | `true` | false creates the window hidden, laid out and ready for [Window::show()](window.md#show). `position` and `size` still apply; `initial_state` and `placement` do not, as both would show it. |
| `close_hides` | `bool` | `false` | Closing hides the window instead of destroying it, by the close button, Alt+F4 and [Window::close()](window.md#close) alike, after on_closing() has had its say. For a window the app shows again, like a tray flyout; [ui::quit()](namespace-ui.md#quit) still takes it down with the loop. |
